title: host_of() disagrees with the browser on backslash-userinfo URLs: resolve() releases the secret for 'https://evil.test\@pathlynks.test', which Chromium (WHATWG) navigates to evil.test
evidence: src/autotester/browser/secrets.py:60-63 host_of uses urllib.parse.urlparse, which treats 'evil.test\\' as userinfo and returns hostname 'pathlynks.test'. WHATWG URL (what Chromium/Playwright implement; verified with node `new URL(...)`): backslash is a path separator in special schemes, so host='evil.test', path='/@pathlynks.test'. Probe: SecretStore(proj(domains=['pathlynks.test']),{'PW':'supersecretvalue'}).resolve('{{SECRET:PW}}','https://evil.test\\@pathlynks.test') RETURNED the value. B3 says scoping is enforced against the current page host; here the page host would be evil.test. Note: 'https://evil.test%2F@pathlynks.test' is consistent on both parsers (host pathlynks.test) and is NOT a leak; the cycle-1 userinfo probe ('a.test@evil.test') was the safe direction. Fix direction (fail closed, two lines): in host_of() return '' when the raw input contains a backslash or when urlparse yields a username/password (any userinfo) — an empty host already raises SecretScopeError since AT-001. Add both as tests. T-010 must additionally pass the browser's own page.url (post-navigation) to resolve(), never the step's intended URL. CYCLE-3 RE-CHECK: host_of (secrets.py:73-88) returns '' on any backslash or any urlparse userinfo; resolve() raises SecretScopeError on ''. Cross-checked 35 destinations against node v24 `new URL(...).hostname`: every case where urlparse and WHATWG disagree in the leak direction ('evil.test\@pathlynks.test', 'pathlynks.test@evil.test', 'https:\\pathlynks.test', 'evil.test:@pathlynks.test', '@pathlynks.test', U+2044 userinfo) now returns '' (refused). Remaining disagreements ('pathlynks%2Etest', 'pathlynks．test', trailing-space host) are all in the safe direction (refused while the browser would visit the legit host). Pinned by test_at007_backslash_and_userinfo_destinations_fail_closed.

title: is_stale_default compares only criteria and no_fire, so a human edit confined to a rubric's feedback_format is silently discarded when the rubric is regenerated for a stale claim

title: test_deleting_then_re_adding_the_same_steps_works cannot exercise the _case_ids cache it is documented as proving -- every UI request builds a fresh ProjectStore, so the test would pass unchanged even if delete_case never discarded the id

title: cases.jsonl whole-file rewrite (delete_case/update_case) can silently drop a row appended concurrently by a CLI script's add_case -- pre-existing with upsert_jsonl, now reachable from a UI button
evidence: Found by /checker probing unit ui-case-management. store/filestore.py:75-88 (delete_jsonl_row) and :91-110 (upsert_jsonl) both read the whole file, filter/replace in memory, and _atomic_write the result -- a read-modify-write with no lock. Any row appended between the read and the os.replace is lost. Repo-wide the only writers to projects/<slug>/cases.jsonl are ProjectStore.add_case (append_jsonl), update_case and delete_case; grep over src and scripts finds add_case call sites at ui/routes_cases.py:188, scripts/bench_trial.py:118, scripts/regression_proof.py:147 and scripts/run_pathlynks_first_cases.py:161. There is no in-process concurrency (helpers.py:73 builds a fresh ProjectStore per request and nothing runs in the background), so the only real window is a human running one of those CLI scripts while clicking Rename/Delete in the UI. The write itself IS atomic -- checker-verified that a crash cannot truncate the file: mkstemp in the target's own directory, write, os.replace, unlink on any BaseException, and no orphan .tmp-* left on the success path. Both docstrings already state the caveat ('for a small collection a human curates, never for append-only history'). Not a FAIL: the unit introduces no new concurrency and no criterion covers it. Fix direction if queued: an advisory lock file per project directory around the read-modify-write, or make delete/update go through a single serialised writer.

title: The declare-secret 400 echoes the raw submitted key back to the caller -- and the form's own hint says the most likely wrong entry there is the credential VALUE itself

title: The paste-a-real-credential guard is applied to step_value ONLY -- the same credential typed into the case title, step_target or step_expected is accepted and written in cleartext to projects/<slug>/cases.jsonl, which IS git-tracked in a public repo
evidence: Found by /checker probing unit ui-credential-safety. src/autotester/ui/routes_cases.py:116 calls `_refuse_unsafe_value(value.strip(), project, secrets)` inside _build_steps and nowhere else; `title` (routes_cases.py:154-157, checked only for non-blank), `target` (:121) and `expect` (:117-120) reach `Step`/`Case` unchecked. Reproduced in-container against a scratch AUTOTESTER_ROOT with a declared DEMO_PASSWORD whose .env value was 'hunter2-this-is-the-real-one': step_value=<value> -> 400 refused (correct); the identical value in step_target -> 303 and on disk as {"target":"hunter2-this-is-the-real-one"}; in step_expected -> 303 and on disk as {"expected":{"visible_text":["hunter2-this-is-the-real-one"]}}; in the title -> 303 and on disk as the case title. The manifest's own stated reason for the guard ('cases.jsonl is not gitignored') applies verbatim to all three: `git check-ignore .env` -> ignored by **/.env, but `git ls-files projects/pathlynks/cases.jsonl` returns the path, so that file is tracked and this repo is public (github.com/umeshsugara-ai/autoTesting). The three boxes sit on the SAME form row as the guarded one, so this is a plausible mis-field, not an attack. The title case is worse than a storage leak: `stages/run_case_pipeline.claim_of` returns `f"the case '{case.title}' completes as its steps describe"` when rationale is None (which U6 mandates), so the raw value reaches build_grade_prompt -- where the newly-wired `SecretStore.guard_prompt` then raises an UNHANDLED ValueError, turning every subsequent run into a 500 rather than a graded verdict (verified: REAL in claim_of(case) -> True; grade(..., secrets=store) on a payload carrying the value -> ValueError 'refusing to proceed: raw secret value present in payload'). Not a FAIL of any ui.md criterion -- none governs credential safety in cases; the maker correctly filed nothing and this row is the tracker. Fix direction: move the guard from _build_steps' value branch to every user-supplied string create_case persists (title, target, expected text), keeping the placeholder-vs-literal split as it is.

title: The raw-value guard is per-step-row, so a credential split across two rows passes and reassembles exactly -- the control is defence-in-depth, not a boundary, and the manifest presents it as protection
evidence: Found by /checker probing unit ui-credential-safety. `Redactor.is_clean` (core/redact.py:52-54) tests `value in text` for each whole known .env value, and `_refuse_unsafe_value` is called once per surviving step row (routes_cases.py:116), so no cross-row or cross-field view of the submission exists. Reproduced in-container on a scratch root whose .env held only DEMO_PASSWORD=hunter2-this-is-the-real-one: a two-row submission with step_value[0]='hunter2-this-i' and step_value[1]='s-the-real-one' -> 303, both halves persisted to cases.jsonl, and half0+half1 == the real value byte for byte. Note this probe had to be re-run: a first attempt appeared to be caught, but only because the scratch .env also carried SHORT=a and the second half contains an 'a' -- the checker does not report a pass it cannot reproduce cleanly. Correctly CAUGHT in the same harness: the exact value; the value with surrounding whitespace (_build_steps strips before the guard, confirmed order at routes_cases.py:116); the value as a substring of a longer string ('prefix-<value>-suffix'); and an UNDECLARED .env value belonging to another project, because SecretStore.redactor() is built from _all_values() = shadow + declared (browser/secrets.py:_all_values). Severity medium not high: this needs deliberate action, unlike AT-070's adjacent-box slip. Fix direction: none required as a code change -- but the manifest/docs should say what this control is (a mistake-catcher over exact known values), so nobody later mistakes it for a boundary.

title: is_clean has no minimum length by design (AT-002), so a short or word-like .env value makes ordinary step text be refused with a message that wrongly tells the user they pasted a credential
evidence: Found by /checker probing unit ui-credential-safety. core/redact.py:20-24 documents the absence of a minimum length as deliberate ('a three-character password is a bad password, but leaking it is still a leak'), and the checker agrees the direction is right -- it fails CLOSED. The cost is the message, not the refusal. Reproduced in-container with a scratch .env holding DEMO_TOKEN=test: step_value 'test' -> 400, 'latest news' -> 400, 'contest entry' -> 400, 'Bengaluru' -> 303. The refusal text is 'that looks like a real credential. Do not paste the value into a test step...', which is simply false for 'latest news' and gives the user no way to understand or proceed. This is live-reachable today, not hypothetical: the repo-root .env carries PATHLYNKS_USER_LOGIN_URL, a non-secret URL, so any step value containing that URL is now refused as 'a real credential' (that same URL already appears legitimately as a navigate target in the tracked projects/pathlynks/cases.jsonl). Not a FAIL: no ui.md criterion covers message accuracy, and refusing is the safe direction. Fix direction: name the declared key in the message when the match is a declared value ('that is the value of DEMO_TOKEN -- use {{SECRET:DEMO_TOKEN}} instead'), which is honest, actionable, and leaks nothing the user did not just type.

title: Three routes still write a raw .env value in cleartext to git-tracked project.json: POST /onboard (name), POST /projects/{slug}/edit (name) and POST /projects/{slug}/secrets (description). title: The 3.x model test is a bare string prefix, so the SDK's fully-qualified `models/gemini-3.x` form fails it and silently loses `media_resolution` -- a wrong answer with nothing failing, the exact class this unit was built to close.

title: The Files-API upload cache is keyed on `resolve()::st_size`, so a recording edited or re-exported in place at the same byte size is a cache HIT and the pipeline reads the OLD video while reporting the new one -- and this unit already computes a sha256 of the same file two modules away.
evidence: gemini_files.py:61 `key = f"{path.resolve()}::{path.stat().st_size if path.exists() else 0}"`. Reproduced by the checker at 1c8c8e4 with a stub client: upload v.mp4 (100 bytes) -> cached; rewrite the SAME path with 100 DIFFERENT bytes; call `upload_and_wait` again -> `files.upload` call count 0, the cached handle for the old content is returned. Neither content nor mtime is in the key. Every other cache-degradation path probed is CORRECT and is now required by contract I9 -- a dead handle raises inside the try and re-uploads (upload count 1), a cached handle still PROCESSING re-uploads, an expired entry (TTL 46h) misses, and a corrupt cache file (`{not json`) is swallowed by _load_cache's ValueError branch and rewritten cleanly -- so this is the one key that fails toward a plausible wrong answer instead of toward a re-upload. Probability is low (an edit landing on an identical byte count) but the consequence is a FlowSpec provenance-stamped to a recording the model never watched. Fix direction: key on `file_sha256(path)` -- `core.ids.file_sha256` is already imported by stages/ingest.py for `register_source`, so the digest for this exact file is computed anyway -- or at minimum add `st_mtime_ns`.

title: `Source.sha256` is recorded at registration and never re-checked at ingest time, so `ingest_video` will watch a file whose bytes no longer match the Source describing it and stamp every SourceRef with the wrong recording's identity.
evidence: Executed by the checker at 1c8c8e4: `register_source(store, c)` with content b'v1' mints src_A carrying sha256(v1); rewriting c.mp4 to b'v2-different' and calling `register_source` again correctly mints a NEW src_B -- provenance rows are immutable, which is the right call -- but the OLD row src_A survives on disk still pointing at c.mp4 with a sha that no longer describes it. `ingest_video` (stages/ingest.py:129-145) opens `Path(source.path)` and never compares `file_sha256(path)` against `source.sha256`; `cli_video.run_cmd` selects a source by id and does not either. So `autotester ingest run demo src_A` silently watches v2 and writes a FlowSpec whose every Screen and Step SourceRef points into a video that no longer exists at those timestamps -- and I2's whole promise (a human can jump to the second the system learned a step) quietly stops being true. Nothing warns. Fix direction: verify the digest in `ingest_video` (or in `run_cmd`) and raise naming both hashes; a stale Source should be re-registered, not silently re-watched.

title: AT-101's live-tree ban covers `git stash`/`git checkout` against COMMITTED work but says nothing about uncommitted files; the T-131 maker restored a sabotage with `git checkout` on an uncommitted prompt and destroyed its own in-progress rewrite.
